<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="100.7.116.115" /></noinclude><section begin="par102" />in the form of an ''ĭ'', attenuated from ''ă'': before a {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}} the prefix takes the vowel of the {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לִפְרִי|translate=for fruit}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּֽאֲרִי|translate=as a lion}}, {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽעֳנִי}} ''bŏʿ<sup>o</sup>nî'', ''in affliction'' (sometimes with the syllable subsequently closed, cf. {{GHGpar|28|b}}, and the infinitives with {{GHGheb|text=לַ}} {{GHGpar|63|i}}): before weak consonants it follows the rule given in {{GHGpar|24|c}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לִֽיהוּדָה}} for {{GHGheb|text=לִיְ׳}}. When the prefixes {{GHGheb|text=בְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְ‍}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, precede {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים|translate=God}}, the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} and {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} regularly coalesce in {{GHGterm|Ṣērê}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽאלֹהִים}}, &c., for {{GHGheb|text=בֶּֽאֱל׳}}; so with suffixes {{GHGheb|text=וֵאֽלֹהָיו}}, &c. (once also in the sing. {{GHGheb|text=לֵֽאלֹהוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=11}}); also regularly {{GHGheb|text=לֵאמֹר|translate=to say}}, for {{GHGheb|text=לֶֽאֱמֹר}}, see {{GHGpar|23|d}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|e}}
(''b'') When the prefixes precede the article, the {{GHGheb|text=ה}} is almost always dropped, and they take its vowel. See further in {{GHGpar|35|n}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|f}}
(''c'') Immediately before the tone-syllable, i.e. before monosyllables and dissyllables with the tone on the penultima (in the fore-tone), they take {{GHGterm|Qameṣ}} (undoubtedly a lengthening of an original ''ă'', cf. {{GHGpar|26|e}}, {{GHGpar|28|a}}), but only in the following cases:

(''aa'') {{GHGheb|text=לָ}} before infinitives of the above-mentioned forms, as {{GHGheb|text=לָתֵת|translate=to give}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָדִין|translate=to judge}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָבֹז|translate=to plunder}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָגֹז|translate=to shear}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָחֹג|translate=to keep a festival}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָלֶ֫דֶת|translate=to bring forth}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָלֶ֫כֶת|translate=to go}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָקַ֫חַת|translate=to take}}, except when the infinitive (as a {{GHGterm|nomen regens}}) is closely connected with another word (especially its subject, {{GHGpar|115|e}}), and consequently, as being in a sort of {{GHGterm|constr. state}}, loses the principal tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְצֵאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=1}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְשֶׁ֫בֶת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=3}}, and so always {{GHGheb|text=לְבֹא חֲמָת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=21}}, &c. (in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=לָֽתֶת־חֶ֫רֶב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=5|verse=21}} the ''ā'' is protected by the secondary tone; before infinitives of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}, the {{GHGheb|text=לָ}} is retained even in close connexion; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=20.25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=22|verse=3|hidebook=1}});

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|g}}
(''bb'') before many pronominal forms, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=בָּזֶה}} (so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=10}}; not {{GHGheb|text=בַּזֶּה}}), {{GHGheb|text=לָזֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּזֶה}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָזֹאת}} (in close connexion, however, {{GHGheb|text=לְזֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}; {{GHGheb|text=כְּזֹאת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=45|verse=23}}); {{GHGheb|text=כָּאֵ֫לֶּה|translate=as these}}; an especially {{GHGheb|text=בָּכֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָכֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּכֶם}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּכֵם}}) and {{GHGheb|text=בָּהֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָהֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּהֵם}} ({{GHGheb|text=כָּהֶם}}), see {{GHGpar|103|e}};

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|h}}
(''cc'') {{GHGheb|text=לָ}} before monosyllables or fore-toned nouns in such combinations as {{GHGheb|text=פֶּה לָפֶה|translate=mouth to month}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=10|verse=21}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֵּין מַ֫יִם לָמָ֫יִם|translate=between waters and waters}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=6}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָטֹ֫רַח|translate=for a trouble}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=14}}, but always before the principal pause. The instructive example in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=8}} also shows that the punctuation {{GHGheb|text=לָ}} is only possible with at least the lesser pause after it; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=10.13}} the {{GHGheb|text=לָ}} is twice repeated, even before the small and smallest disjunctives;

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|i}}
(''dd'') in certain standing expressions, which have become stereotyped almost as adverbs, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לָעַד|translate=to eternity}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָרֹב|translate=in multitude}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָבֶ֫טַח|translate=in security}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָנֶ֫צַח|translate=to eternity}}, but {{GHGheb|text=לְנֵ֫צַח נְצָחִים|translate=to all eternity}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=10}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=לָנֶ֫פֶשׁ|translate=for the dead}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=19|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=9|verse=10|hidebook=1}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|k}}
(''d'') With the interrogative {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} they are pointed as in {{GHGheb|text=בַּמֶּה}}; in {{GHGterm|pause}} and before {{GHGheb|text=א}} as in {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּה|translate=by what?}} (before a following relative clause, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=3|verse=22}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּמֶה}}; cf. Delitzsch, ''Jesaia'', 4th ed., on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=22}}); {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּה|translate=how much}}? but also {{GHGheb|text=כַּמֶּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=22|verse=16}}, in close connexion, and at a greater distance from the {{GHGterm|pause}}. The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} in these forms arises from a modification of the original ''ă'', while the {{GHGheb|text=מ‍}} is sharpened in order to maintain the original ''ǎ'' of the prefixes.

{{GHGmargin-letter|102|l}}
When {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} (prop. ''la'') is united to {{GHGheb|text=מָה}}, it takes, according to {{GHGpar|49|f}}, g, the form {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָה}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=8}} {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מֶה}}, all {{GHGterm|Milʿêl}}, and hence the ''ă'' in the tone is lengthened to ''ā'') ''for what? why?'' Before the gutturals {{GHGheb|text=א}}, {{GHGheb|text=ה}}, {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָמָ֫ה}} is used for euphonic reasons (exceptions {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=14|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=15|verse=18}}, before {{GHGheb|text=ה}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=22}},<section end="par102" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
